sections.title: P1-Q6 — Обязательные атрибуты конверта события (CloudEvents)
sections.text:
**Запрос:** `CloudEvents specification required context attributes for event envelopes (id, source, type, specversion, time, subject) and guidance on event type versioning. Explain in prose why published integration event schemas need explicit versioning separate from internal class names.`

**Статус:** success-partial — провайдер вернул **только таблицу**; прозаическое объяснение
«почему версия схемы отделена от имени класса» не пришло и остаётся обоснованным
таблицей P1-Q5 (строка Integration event) плюс строкой `type` этой таблицы.
**Источники:** github.com (cloudevents/spec) — цитируется провайдером построчно, отдельного
списка URL в усечённом ответе нет.

**Захват (дословно):**

| Attribute | Requirement | Purpose | Practical guidance |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `id` | Required | Identifies this specific event | Make `source` + `id` unique for every distinct published event. Persist or derive it deterministically where consumers need idempotency. |
| `source` | Required | Identifies the producer context in which the occurrence happened | Use a stable URI-reference-like identifier, such as `urn:acme:school-platform:enrollment`. It is a producer/domain identity, not necessarily a host URL. |
| `type` | Required | Names the kind of business occurrence | Use a stable, public contract identifier such as `com.acme.enrollment.student-enrolled.v1`. Consumers commonly route, authorize, observe, and dispatch using this field. |
| `specversion` | Required | States the CloudEvents envelope specification version | Usually `1.0`. This tells infrastructure how to interpret the CloudEvents metadata; **it is not your payload or domain-event schema version.** |
| `time` | Optional | Timestamp when the business occurrence happened | Include it whenever known. If the actual occurrence time is unavailable, a producer may use another time, but producers for the same `source` should apply that policy consistently. |
| `subject` | Optional | Identifies the entity affected, in the context of `source` | Use a stable, filter-friendly identifier such as `students/8b42…`. It helps generic infrastructure filter without deserializing the payload. |

---

sections.title: P1-Q7 — Как архитектурный документ перестаёт расходиться с кодом
sections.text:
**Запрос:** `How to stop an architecture guidelines document from drifting out of sync with the codebase: architecture fitness functions, executable architecture rules in CI, relationship between ADRs and a living architecture handbook, and the rule that each normative statement has exactly one owning document. Explain in prose with concrete practices.`

**Статус:** success · **Источники:** github.com/architecture-decision-record/architecture-decision-record

**Захват — диагноз:**

> Architecture documents drift when they try to be both a timeless explanation, a decision log,
> and a rulebook — while the code changes without a mechanism that detects contradiction.
> Prevent drift by **separating those roles**, making important constraints **executable in
> CI**, and assigning every normative statement **one canonical home**.

**Fitness function — определение и обязательные поля:**

> An architecture fitness function is an objective check that assesses whether the system still
> has an architectural property you care about. It can be a static dependency test, a contract
> test, a deployment-policy check, a runtime SLO check, or even a periodically performed review
> — but the most valuable ones run automatically and frequently.

> Do not write "the system must preserve tenant isolation" only in a handbook. Write it in the
> handbook **and** express the observable parts as checks that fail when isolation is broken.
> Not every architectural idea is fully machine-verifiable. But almost every important rule has
> some testable surface area.

> A fitness function should state: **Characteristic protected** … **Scope** … **Measurement**
> — the command, query, test, monitor, or review procedure … **Threshold** — pass/fail
> criterion, not "keep it reasonable" … **Cadence** — PR, merge-to-main, deploy, nightly,
> weekly, or quarterly … **Owner** — team or role accountable … **Linked decision** — ADR(s) or
> handbook section explaining why it exists.

> This avoids vague architecture claims such as "keep coupling low." A useful replacement is:
> "Billing may depend on `Contracts\Orders`, but not on `Orders\Internal`, `Orders\Models`, or
> the orders database tables; the dependency test runs on every pull request."

**Разные роли ADR и справочника:**

> An ADR is a decision record: it captures an architecturally significant decision, its context,
> alternatives, decision, consequences, and lifecycle status such as proposed, accepted, or
> superseded. It explains **how the system acquired its current shape**; it is not the best
> place to maintain an always-current operational rulebook.
> A living architecture handbook is a **current-state guide**. It should answer questions a
> contributor has today: What are the system's modules and ownership boundaries? Which
> integration paths are permitted? Which data is owned by whom? Which APIs/events are public
> contracts? … Where are the executable checks, and how can a developer run them locally?

Названный паттерн связи: ADR → handbook section and enforcement test/path; handbook rule →
ADR rationale and CI command; test metadata/comment → handbook rule identifier and ADR number.

**Форма правила со стабильным идентификатором** `[листинг сокращён]`:

> `Handbook rule: MOD-004` · `Rule:` A module may consume another module only through its
> public Contracts or Events namespace. Internal namespaces and owned tables are forbidden. ·
> `Rationale:` ADR-0007, ADR-0014 · `Enforcement:` конкретные команды · `Exceptions:`
> `docs/architecture/exceptions/MOD-004/*.md`

> This creates an auditable triangle: **decision → present rule → executable assurance.**

**Правило одного владельца (дословно):**

> Every normative statement — every "must," "must not," "only," "required," or "prohibited" —
> has exactly one canonical source. Other documents may summarize or link to it, but they must
> not independently restate the rule as authoritative prose. Otherwise, two pages eventually
> disagree and readers cannot know which one governs.

> The source owner need not always be the handbook. For example, "the `student.enrolled.v1`
> event has field `tenant_id`" should be owned by the **event schema**, not duplicated as
> normative truth in an ADR or handbook.

Форма не-владеющей ссылки, названная ответом:

> Wrong, in the ADR: "All migrations must follow expand–migrate–contract."
> Better: "This decision relies on the current database-change policy, owned by
> `handbook/deployment-compatibility.md#DB-003`."

> Use stable identifiers such as `MOD-004`, `DATA-009`, or `DEP-003`. Identifiers make links
> resilient to document reorganization and let CI messages be precise:
> `Architecture policy MOD-004 failed: Enrollment\Actions\ApproveEnrollment imports
> Identity\Internal\RiskEngine. Use Identity\Contracts\RiskAssessment instead, or change
> MOD-004 through an ADR.`

**Как это поддерживается процессом (дословный перечень):**

> - Add a CODEOWNERS rule for `docs/architecture/**` and architecture-policy test directories.
> - Run a documentation link checker and fail on broken ADR/rule/test references.
> - Maintain a small **rule registry** — YAML, JSON, or Markdown front matter — with rule ID,
>   owner path, scope, enforcement command, ADR links, team owner, and review date.
> - Have CI validate that each handbook rule marked `enforcement: automated` points to a real
>   command or test target.
> - Have CI flag architecture-test changes that remove a rule without updating the linked
>   handbook/ADR.
> - Generate dependency graphs, package maps, API inventories, or schema ownership reports from
>   source. **Generated output is evidence, not canonical prose.**
> - Make exceptions explicit, narrow, and expiring. An exception should name the violated rule,
>   affected paths, owner, reason, compensating controls, expiry date, and removal issue.

> The PR should be rejected when either half is missing: code changes an enforced architectural
> rule but not its decision/documentation; documentation changes a normative rule but not its
> corresponding executable enforcement — **or explicitly states why enforcement is not
> automatable.**

> A useful exception record is not "legacy code is exempt." It is: `EXC-0017: … until
> 2026-11-30, because migration MIG-482 is in progress. No new callers allowed. Owner: Billing
> team. Removal verification: DatabaseOwnershipTest.`

Финальная формулировка:

> The goal is not maximal documentation. It is a tight feedback loop: ADRs preserve reasoning,
> the handbook declares present obligations, CI enforces the mechanically verifiable ones, and
> exceptions expose the gap until it is removed.

---

sections.title: P1-Q8 — Словарь суффиксов имён и generic-антипаттерны
sections.text:
**Запрос:** `Why are class names like Manager, Helper, Util, Info, Data, Common and Processor considered naming antipatterns in object-oriented design, and what precise suffix vocabulary do experienced PHP and Laravel teams recommend instead (Factory, Repository, Resolver, Builder, Policy, Registry, Provider)? Explain in prose with the criterion for when a suffix is meaningful.`

**Статус:** success-no-sources — содержательный синтез **без списка URL**. Используется как
подтверждение общей практики, но не как единственное основание запрета.

**Захват — критерий:**

> Names such as `Manager`, `Helper`, `Util`, `Info`, `Data`, `Common`, and bare `Processor` are
> usually antipatterns because they classify code by **vagueness, not by responsibility**. …
> A suffix is meaningful only when it makes a **falsifiable promise** about the class's role:
> from the name alone, a developer should be able to predict its public API, dependencies,
> ownership boundaries, and reason to change. If almost any collection of methods could fit the
> name, the suffix is not doing useful design work.

> The core problem is not that these words are forbidden English. The problem is that they
> weaken discovery and review … New work gets appended to the generic bucket because its name
> has no **exclusion rule**.

Эмпирическая ссылка (без URL в ответе):

> a study of open-source Java code found classes ending in `-Utils` and generic actor suffixes
> correlated with substantially higher complexity and lower cohesion than other class groups.
> That does not prove every utility class is bad, but it matches the architectural intuition.

**Тест на пригодность суффикса (дословно):**

> Use a suffix only if it answers a specific question about the class: *What exact
> responsibility does this object have, and what would make code inappropriate to add to it?*
> A good suffix supplies both a **positive contract and a negative boundary.**
> … Read the class name without opening it. Predict its verbs and dependencies. Open the class.
> If its methods, injected collaborators, and side effects surprise you, the suffix is probably
> too broad. Ask whether a proposed new method is clearly in or clearly out. If the answer is
> "it could go either way," rename or split the class.

> The noun before the suffix must also be precise. `PaymentProvider` is still ambiguous if
> "provider" could mean a Laravel service provider, a third-party payment gateway, or a domain
> supplier.

**Названные исключения (дословно):**

> These words are smells, **not bans**.
> - `Provider` is a first-class Laravel term. `AppServiceProvider` is precise because Laravel
>   defines its lifecycle and expected `register()`/`boot()` responsibilities.
> - `Manager` can be legitimate when it is an established, narrow technical term with a
>   documented lifecycle — such as a framework-owned queue manager or connection manager. Still,
>   a name like `DatabaseConnectionManager` is materially better than `Manager`.
> - `Helper` can be acceptable for narrowly scoped framework view helpers or a small set of
>   global pure functions … that does not justify an application-wide `Helpers` namespace.
> - `Data` may be appropriate in a deliberate DTO convention, **but only if your team
>   standardizes the semantic role** … In many applications, `CreateStudentInput`,
>   `StudentResponse`, or `StudentSummary` communicates the direction and lifecycle more clearly.
> - `Processor` is acceptable when the domain really has a well-defined processing protocol and
>   the object's input/output are evident … A bare `Processor` is not.

**Предложенное командное правило:**

> Name the domain or technical concept first; add a role suffix only when it identifies a
> stable responsibility, expected collaboration pattern, and clear exclusion boundary.

> Avoid replacing every vague name with `Service`. **`Service` is often just `Manager` with
> better branding** unless the team has a documented meaning for it … The real goal is not
> suffix purity; it is code whose filename accurately predicts its responsibility and makes
> misplaced behavior visibly out of place.

---

sections.title: P1-Q9 — Профили структуры: слой, фича, bounded context
sections.text:
**Запрос:** `Package by layer versus package by feature versus bounded-context-first directory structure: at what codebase size does layer-first grouping stop working, what guidance exists on the number of direct children of a source root, and why single-class directories are considered noise. Explain in prose with concrete thresholds used in practice.`

**Статус:** success-partial — провайдер вернул **только таблицу**. Числовые пороги
(сколько прямых детей корня, при каком размере слой-первая группировка перестаёт работать) и
аргумент про каталог из одного класса **не получены**. Пункты дизайна, которые они должны
были подтвердить, несут `[UNVERIFIED]` на внешней части и опираются на измеренное
распределение из `@plan/knowledge/research-00-baseline-metrics.json` §1 (`RAG:—`).
**Источники:** не перечислены провайдером в усечённом ответе.

**Захват (дословно):**

| Structure | Top-level organization | Best fit | Primary failure mode |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Package by layer | `Controllers/`, `Services/`, `Models/`, `Repositories/` | Small application, prototype, simple CRUD with one coherent domain | A single feature is physically scattered across every technical folder |
| Package by feature | `Billing/`, `Enrollment/`, `Scheduling/` | Most product applications and modular monoliths | Shared/cross-cutting code becomes a dumping ground unless governed |
| Bounded-context-first | `Identity/`, `Academics/`, `Billing/`, each containing features and layers | Larger product domains, multiple teams, independent terminology/lifecycles | Premature fragmentation if "contexts" are merely nouns or database tables |
